summary: Kaiun Shiradate was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught Takanori Unno and Fujio Taniguchi, and served at Otani University as a lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and later as a professor (attested 1999–2002).

Kakichi Kadowaki (1926–2017) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Sogen Omori, and held a post at Sophia University from around 1960 to 1996.
Kakushō Ujiie (d. 1985) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tribhuvan University (attested 1970). He served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1970 and 1984–1985).

Kalidas Nag (1891–1966) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Scottish Church College (~1908–1912) and the University of Calcutta (~1912–1914), taught at Scottish Church College (~1914–1919) and Calcutta (~1923–1955), and founded the Greater India Society in 1926.

Kalu Rinpoche (1905–1989) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Osel Ling under teachers including Lama Norbu Tondrup. He served as Vajra Master at Palpung (~1940–1955) and Abbot at Changchub Choeling (1957).
Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is a scholar in Indology and Sinology who studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He served as an emeritus professor at the University of Windsor (attested 2002).

Kamala Tiyavanich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, later holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there in 1993–1994.

Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Bonn (~1969–1970), the University of Toronto (~1971–1972), and Brown University (~1974–1975).

Kamil Václav Zvelebil (1927–2009) specialized in Indology and linguistics. After earning his PhD at Charles University (1946–1952), he held posts at the Oriental Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Charles University, and Utrecht University (~1976–1992).

Kamla Chowdhry (1920–2006) studied at Santiniketan, University of the Punjab, University of Calcutta, and Michigan State University. She held posts at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (~1962–1972) and Harvard University (~1968–1969).

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi (1935–2021) was an Indologist who studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University (~1995–2021), Chairman of Kalidasa Akademi, and Advisor at Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 2009).

Kammie Takahashi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano and Paul Groner, holding a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.
Kan Hang (b. 1965) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Su Bai and has served as the head of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.

Kanai Lal Hazra (b. 1932) specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and completed a PhD under Sirima Kiribamune at the University of Ceylon (~1964–1968), later lecturing in Pali at Calcutta (attested 1982).
Kanchu Onoue is a Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as a teacher at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and as a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).

Kang-nam Oh works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yun-hua Jan (attested 1976), later holding a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).
Kang-yuan Sung specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Calgary (attested 1999) under MA supervisor Anthony W. Barber and teacher Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie, attended the University of Paris, and held a non-regular appointment at the Tokyo Imperial Household Museum.
Kanoko Tanaka specializes in religious studies and Indology. She studied under Acharya Tulsi and served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1962) and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1962).
